chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Zakariyya ibn Adam who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)

about the dog and the cheetah (leopard) when they are sent out and kill [prey], he said to me, 'They are among those referred to by Allah, the Exalted, in the word 'Mukallibin' (hunting dogs), so there is no harm in eating them.'

key_terms.يُرْسَلاَنِ: When they are sent out (for hunting)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat meat killed by a cheetah or dog according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) validates the permissibility of consuming prey killed by hunting dogs and cheetahs by linking them to the Quranic term 'Mukallibin' (those who teach hunting) in Surah Al-Ma'idah. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of extending the specific category of trained hunting dogs to other similar predatory animals used for sport, emphasizing the role of human training in rendering the animal's catch lawful.
